1.explanation: All three classes (Item, PopupItem, SubNav) implement icon-only behavior in their render() methods. They each detect iconOnly in context and, when no icon is provided, insert a placeholder element (`<span className="...nav-icon-placeholder" />`). This placeholder causes empty blanks for items without icons. To fix the bug, these render methods must skip rendering the placeholder for items that lack an explicit icon when iconOnly=true, so that only items with icons reserve space.
1.bug_scenario: In iconOnly mode on a vertical Nav, items that do not have an explicit icon configured still render an empty placeholder span (producing a blank row or blank icon cell). According to the spec, un-iconed items should not occupy icon space when iconOnly=true, but today they leave an empty slot, resulting in visible blanks in the menu (as shown in the screenshot).

2.explanation: All three classes (Item, PopupItem and SubNav) include logic in their render methods that, when iconOnly is true and no icon prop is provided, unconditionally inserts a <span className="nav-icon-placeholder"/>. This is what creates the empty gap. To fix the bug, the placeholder insertion should be gated (or removed) for cases where no icon was configured, so that items without an icon simply render without any extra placeholder space.
2.bug_scenario: In iconOnly mode on a vertical Nav, any Nav.Item, Nav.PopupItem or Nav.SubNav without an explicitly provided icon still renders an empty placeholder (a blank “ghost” icon area). According to the spec (“iconOnly 模式下未配置icon的项不应出现空白”), items without an icon prop should simply collapse (no gap), not show a blank placeholder.
